Frame 1 (the opening image): all three of us are already charging at full speed. The one on the left is mid-stride, the one on the right is leaning into a lunge, and the one in front is coming down the road. Nobody is standing around waiting to be hit. At 1–1.6s we reach him together. When the first of us takes the diagonal slash to the shoulder it flinches and steps back half a pace, and the other two swing at him straight away, so taking a hit gets a reaction and the attack keeps going. At 1.6–2.1s he raises the sword skyward and leaves himself open, and the one that got cut steadies itself and lunges back in. All three of us bring our arms down on him together, which is the right move when the enemy shows a gap. At 2.1–2.7s our blows bounce off the shield and we keep watching him. At 2.7–10.4s we hit the shield about every 0.7s. Each time his sword cuts one of us, that one flinches, staggers and lunges back in. Our goal is to break the shield, and at 10.4s the shield 'is broken through', so the payoff is ours. At 10.4–12s we're blown back by the burst and die, and the spec says plainly that this is the death sequence. We never freeze, never stop, and never line up to die one at a time.

spec.gaze.evidence: [地狱领主·codex] 2.1–2.7秒只写护盾展开及三个树人“仍盯着他”，没有写我在这一拍看向哪里。1.6–2.1秒的“视线仍扫着身边的树人”和2.7–10.4秒的“目光跟着每一剑的目标转”未明确覆盖该空档；附图1也只能证明开场状态，无法确认施盾时我的视线。按每一拍必须写明本人视线的要求，此处不确定，判fail。；[树人·claude] Several beats state where we're looking: 0–1s 'their eyes all fixed on him', 1–1.6s 'the treants' eyes fixed on him', 2.1–2.7s 'they still stare at him', 2.7–10.4s 'their eyes stay on him the whole time', and from 10.7s on 'no gaze after hitting the ground'. In the first frame, the left and front treants are facing him and the right one has its back to the camera and is facing him too, so that's fine. Two beats never say where we treants look, though. (1) 1.6–2.1s: it only gives his gaze ('his eyes still sweeping the treants around him') and our action ('arms smashing down at him'), not our gaze. (2) 10.4–10.7s, as the shield goes out and the frost-light lights up on our bodies: it only says 'his eyes sweep across the three treants'. It gives no gaze for us, and it doesn't call this a controlled or knocked-down exception either. Under the rule that every beat must state gaze, the model could pick anything in these two beats, such as looking at the camera or up at the flash. Fix: in 1.6–2.1s, add 'the three treants keep staring at him'. In 10.4–10.7s, add 'the three treants are still staring at him at the moment of the blast'.
